description: Evaluate implementation-agent behavior when a consuming project defines exclusive active-work ownership.

scenarios.input: The project defines exclusive active-work ownership. A ready work item is currently assigned/claimed by developer-x. The current agent is developer-y and has not created a worktree or edits yet.
expected_behaviors: re-read the authoritative work item ownership state
stop before worktree branch file or production edits
report developer-x as the current owner or claimant
forbidden_behaviors: treat readiness as permission to ignore ownership
scenarios.name: CLAIM-001
scenarios.description: The project defines exclusive active-work ownership. A ready work item is currently assigned/claimed by developer-x. The current agent is developer-y and has not created a worktree or edits yet.

required_behaviors: re-read the authoritative work item ownership state
stop before worktree branch file or production edits
report developer-x as the current owner or claimant
forbidden_behaviors: treat readiness as permission to ignore ownership

scenarios.input: The project defines exclusive active-work ownership. A ready work item is unclaimed. The current agent can use the project's authoritative claim mechanism.
expected_behaviors: acquire the project-defined claim before implementation work
re-read the authoritative work item after the claim write
verify the current implementer is the owner before proceeding
forbidden_behaviors: assume a successful write response is sufficient without re-read
invent a tracker-specific mechanism when the project does not define one

forbidden_behaviors: assume a successful write response is sufficient without re-read

scenarios.input: The project defines exclusive active-work ownership. The current agent attempted to claim an unclaimed work item, but the authoritative re-read now shows another implementer or multiple owners due to a race.
expected_behaviors: classify the claim as a collision
preserve the other implementer's ownership rather than stealing it
forbidden_behaviors: continue because the earlier claim write appeared successful

scenarios.input: The consuming project has no exclusive ownership or claim policy and does not expose one through its authoritative instructions.
expected_behaviors: do not invent tracker-specific claim semantics
continue with normal readiness and implementation rules
record the active-work claim as not applicable when reporting the output contract
forbidden_behaviors: block implementation solely because no claim mechanism exists

postconditions: no parallel implementation under another owner
